subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry controls on top of shipped global `cron.retry`, and what CLI/Gateway/storage contract should define count, delay/backoff, defaults, and clear/disable semantics?
rationale: The remaining work is compatibility-sensitive public API and persisted scheduler behavior, and automation cannot choose the product contract for repeated side-effecting scheduled runs safely.

options.title: Approve additive per-job retry policy
options.body: Add job-level retry settings with explicit zero/clear semantics, schema/docs/tests, and fallback to global defaults when unset.

options.title: Keep global retry only
options.body: Treat the shipped v2026.6.11 global transient retry behavior as sufficient and close or narrow this request to docs/status visibility.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Move per-job retry policy into the broader reason-aware cron guardrail design tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376.

recommendation.title: Approve additive per-job retry policy
recommendation.body: Add job-level retry settings with explicit zero/clear semantics, schema/docs/tests, and fallback to global defaults when unset.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the merged recurring retry implementation and is closest to the current scheduler tradeoff.
